clue.text: Live a dull life when victory sign is out of reach

parts.words: Live a dull life when victory sign is out of reach
parts.note: surface reading: someone idles away the days because triumph seems unattainable

parts.words: victory sign is out of reach
parts.note: setter's reading: the V-sign starts the word, and what is out of reach is something you cannot get at

explanation.surface: A defeated soul sinks into a dreary existence once winning looks impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as V, E, GET AT, E: a playful nod to the victory V and to a thing one cannot get at. The wordplay is loose, so the definition does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To vegetate is to live an inactive, monotonous existence, like a plant doing nothing but growing.

clue.text: Grabbing a copper in France you look so dumb

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so the outer word wraps round the rest

parts.note: the French word for you
taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A tourist in France stares blankly while being grabbed by a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman; here it is the metal, Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacuous means empty-headed and lacking intelligence, a common sense of dumb meaning stupid.

clue.text: Tricky feat for Q's followers in the old county

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: abbreviation for Glamorgan, a Welsh county abolished in 1974
the letters after Q in the alphabet, read as R and S

explanation.surface: A difficult stunt is pulled off by Q's successors in a former county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Q's followers' looks like disciples of someone called Q; it is the next two letters of the alphabet, joined by and.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand slam, winning every trick in bridge or every major title in a sport, is a notably hard feat.

clue.text: Land appears to soak up the downpour

parts.words: Land appears to soak up the downpour
parts.note: surface reading: the ground absorbs a heavy shower of rain

parts.words: appears to soak up the downpour
parts.note: setter's reading: the word for land looks as if it holds the downpour within it

explanation.surface: After a storm, the ground drinks in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: TERRAIN ends with RAIN, and read aloud it is close to 'the rain', so the land seems to have taken up the downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features, such as hills or ground conditions.

clue.text: Volume about pig-raising — not a game for many

indicators.note: about means going round, so the volume encloses the other piece

parts.note: a tome is a large book or volume

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word upward, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A book about pig farming, which is hardly a party game.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a game or activity for two players, such as a two-ball round of golf, rather than for a crowd.

clue.text: Swaggering walk with which a couple can change direction

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the word before it has its letters rearranged

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair, a couple
the three letters of can rearranged
E for east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A strutting step that lets a dancing pair turn about on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To prance is to move with high, springy, showy steps, a strutting gait full of self-display.

clue.text: Everything's divine, he says

definitions.note: a person: the one who says this

parts.note: surface reading: someone gushes that it is all simply marvellous
setter's reading: the speaker believes God is in all things, the creed that identifies the deity with the universe

explanation.surface: A man enthusing that everything is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' sounds like a gushing compliment; it is meant literally. The word also splits as PAN, Greek for all, and THEIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheist holds that God and the universe are identical, so all things are divine.

clue.text: He prosecutes an employer of 200

parts.note: the indefinite article
CC is the Roman numeral for 200
one who employs something uses it

explanation.surface: A lawyer pursuing a case against a boss with a staff of two hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employer' suggests a boss with staff; it means one who employs, or uses, a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser brings a charge against someone, which is what a prosecutor does in court.

clue.text: This could wound a girl

parts.note: to wound with a blade is to cut
lass is a northern and Scottish word for a girl

explanation.surface: A warning that this weapon might injure a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a weapon, and the words wound and a girl also build it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword once used by sailors, so it is something that could wound anyone.

clue.text: Mrs Mopp receives one as president

indicators.note: whoever receives something takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Mrs Mopp was the office cleaner in the wartime BBC radio comedy ITMA
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is handed a role as head of the organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: A charwoman is a cleaner; Mrs Mopp, from the 1940s radio show ITMA, became the byword for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairwoman presides over a meeting or board, so she acts as its president or head.

clue.text: Sound sense to quote

indicators.note: Sound tells us the word that follows is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Common sense is a good thing to have on your side when quoting.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to quote a passage or refer to an authority as evidence or support.

clue.text: Ancient Mariner a pain in the neck as related by Scheherezade

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a veteran seafarer, read literally

definitions.text: a pain in the neck as related by Scheherezade
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the creature in the Sinbad tale of the Arabian Nights who rode on Sinbad's shoulders and would not get off

explanation.surface: Coleridge's old sailor gets confused with a burdensome figure from the Arabian Nights.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fifth voyage of Sinbad, told by Scheherazade, the Old Man of the Sea clings round his neck; the phrase now means a burden one cannot shake off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes an aged sailor and idiomatically means a persistent burden, from the creature that clung to Sinbad's shoulders.

clue.text: Hamlet's last golden utterance

definitions.note: his dying words are The rest is silence
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the closing word of Hamlet's dying line, The rest is
second meaning: the proverb says speech is silver but this is golden

explanation.surface: The prince's final speech is praised as a priceless piece of eloquence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utterance' is ironic: the golden thing in the proverb is saying nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet dies saying The rest is silence, and the proverb holds that saying nothing is golden.

clue.text: Vivid description of an artist's palette

definitions.meaning: second meaning: literally full of colour, as a painter's mixing board is

explanation.surface: A lively account of the board a painter mixes colours on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Description' looks like a noun to define; it says the answer is a word that would describe the palette.
explanation.definitionFit: Colourful means full of bright colours and, figuratively, lively and vivid, as a painter's paint-smeared board is.

clue.text: A nobody such as Evelyn?

definitions.note: Charles Pooter, of The Diary of a Nobody
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the hero of the Grossmiths' comic novel The Diary of a Nobody kept a journal
second meaning: John Evelyn kept a famous seventeenth-century journal

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person called Evelyn is a nonentity.
explanation.walkthrough: Evelyn looks like a first name; it is John Evelyn, contemporary of Pepys. The Nobody is Mr Pooter of The Diary of a Nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: A diarist keeps a daily journal, as John Evelyn did and as the fictional Pooter did in The Diary of a Nobody.

clue.text: Maybe treating 4's tail to make it whole?

indicators.note: maybe hints that the word is only one possible form of its letters, which can be reordered

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

indicators.note: a tail is the end, so only the final letter of the referenced entry is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the answer to 4 down

explanation.surface: A query about whether medical treatment of an injured tail will make it whole again.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 4 down is TWOSOME, whose last letter E joins the letters of treating.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to combine parts into a complete unit, literally to make something entire.

clue.text: Put together first of many held by police at random

indicators.note: at random means in no fixed order, so the letters are scrambled
something held by another is gripped inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the six letters of police mixed up

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter of many

explanation.surface: The first of many suspects is rounded up by officers in an arbitrary sweep.
explanation.definitionFit: To compile is to collect material and assemble it into a single list, book or whole.

clue.text: Strife among dons changed the way ahead

definitions.note: an adverb: forward, the way ahead

indicators.note: something changed is altered, so the letters are put in a new order
among places one piece in the middle of the other

parts.note: the letters of dons rearranged
war is armed strife

explanation.surface: Conflict among university fellows reshaped the college's path forward.
explanation.walkthrough: Dons are Oxford and Cambridge teaching fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: Onwards means forward in space or time, which is the direction that lies ahead.

clue.text: Flourishing, the sun-god, in the old Syrian city

parts.note: palmy days are prosperous, flourishing ones
Ra was the Egyptian sun-god

explanation.surface: A sun-god's cult thrives in an ancient city of Syria.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmyra was an ancient caravan city in the Syrian desert, famous for its ruins and Queen Zenobia.

clue.text: Race official for opening course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the person who fires the gun to begin a race
second meaning: the first dish of a meal

explanation.surface: An official at a race meeting sets out for the first part of the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a racecourse, but it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of beginning: the official begins the race, the dish begins the dinner.

clue.text: Hair-do seen on the beach

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short tapered haircut fashionable in the 1920s
second meaning: the pebbles covering a beach

explanation.surface: A hairstyle spotted at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: A shingle was a short bobbed cut tapering at the nape, and shingle is also loose rounded pebbles on a shore.

clue.text: Such an eclipse to invalidate a king

parts.note: to annul is to declare void
taken as written
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An eclipse that sweeps a monarch from power.
explanation.definitionFit: In an annular eclipse the moon leaves a ring of sun visible around it, from Latin anulus, a ring.

clue.text: As sentries do their beats — tired with this, it's said?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: guards walk over the same route again and again
second meaning: a wheel fitted with this is tyred, which is how tired sounds

explanation.surface: Sentries pacing their rounds grow weary of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired' is a pun on tyred: a remoulded tyre is called by the answer, so a wheel 'tyred with this' wears one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentries tread their beats over and over, and a remoulded tyre with new tread is a well-known noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Singular piano composition in the isle — The Witching Time

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the island's name

parts.note: the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast

indicators.note: a composition is something put together anew, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: singular as written, plus P, the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: An odd piano piece set on an island, titled after the hour of witches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The isle' alone means Wight to a British solver, as the Isle of Wight. Walpurgis Night, 30 April, is when witches gather in German folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: Walpurgis Night, the eve of May Day, is the traditional night of the witches' sabbath in German folklore.

clue.text: Living here enjoyed by a trimmer — seems to sound asinine

definitions.text: Living here enjoyed by a trimmer
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Berkshire parish of the song The Vicar of ..., whose vicar kept his living by changing sides
second meaning: to make a donkey's cry

explanation.surface: A turncoat's comfortable home life looks as foolish as a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: A living is a parish post held by a clergyman, and a trimmer is someone who shifts with the political wind, like the Vicar of Bray in the old song.
explanation.definitionFit: To bray is to make the loud harsh cry of a donkey, and an ass is a donkey.

clue.text: Flog standard measure tea mixture

indicators.note: a mixture has its ingredients stirred together, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner
an old cloth measure of about 45 inches
the three letters of tea scrambled

explanation.surface: An order to beat out a regular quantity of a tea blend.
explanation.definitionFit: To flagellate is to whip or scourge, which is what flogging someone means.

clue.text: Attack very musical student

parts.note: assai is the Italian musical direction for very, as in allegro assai
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone launches into a highly musical pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very musical' reads as praise of the student, but it is the musical word for very.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently, physically or with words.

clue.text: Give help to Old Contemptibles unhappily in red

indicators.note: unhappily suggests things are out of sorts, so the words after it are disordered

parts.note: the Old Contemptibles were the British Expeditionary Force of 1914
the five letters of in red rearranged

explanation.surface: Coming to the aid of the miserable old soldiers dressed in red.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Contemptibles took their name from the Kaiser's reported sneer at Britain's contemptible little army of 1914.
explanation.definitionFit: To befriend someone is to act as a friend to them, offering kindness and support.
